headline: South Asia: 'Fake and fabricated': Info ministry rejects NYT report claiming PAF jets being used against Yemen's Houthis
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

- South Asia: 'Fake and fabricated': Info ministry rejects NYT report claiming PAF jets being used against Yemen's Houthis.

- Asia: At least 33 dead in Russian bomb blast in east Ukraine stronghold.

Full breakdown follows.

- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: ‘Cushy office’ scale down - Civil society advocates question Gov’t decision-making as backlash leads to pull back on NaRRA office space . PM warns adjustment will slow roll-out of projects, impact delivery.
The Government’s decision to scale down the office space that will house the National Reconstruction and Resilience Authority (NaRRA) and cut rental costs, though welcomed, is raising questions about the quality of analysis behind government lease agreements, civil society advocate Carol Narcisse has said. “The decision-making clearly has to be more thoughtful about identifying needs and making sure that what we are expending is commensurate with what is needed and what is sufficient,” Narcisse told The Gleaner yesterday.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Walk for the Cure returns amid mammography crisis.
Jamaicans are being urged to turn cancer awareness into action by participating in the 15th staging of CIBC Caribbean’s Walk for the Cure at Hope Botanical Gardens on Sunday. The event, being held in partnership with the Jamaica Cancer Society (JCS), comes as the society faces an urgent need for more than $35 million to replace its only mammogram machine, which has been out of service since August 29. The 2026 staging is being held under the theme ‘One Caribbean. One Mission. Communities Walking for Change’, with a focus on cancer awareness, screening, treatment and care.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Ali warns Caribbean to scale up or risk being left behind.
GEORGETOWN, Guyana: Guyana’s President Dr Mohamed Irfaan Ali has warned Caribbean tourism leaders to “scale up” or risk being left behind as destinations in the Middle East and Latin America pour billions into tourism infrastructure and development. Ali said the Caribbean could no longer depend primarily on its beaches, natural beauty and established global appeal, arguing that the next phase of tourism must be driven by larger and smarter investments in transportation, resilience, technology, visitor experiences and regional integration.

South Asia - bottom line: 'Fake and fabricated': Info ministry rejects NYT report claiming PAF jets being used against Yemen's Houthis.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: 'Fake and fabricated': Info ministry rejects NYT report claiming PAF jets being used against Yemen's Houthis.
The Ministry of Information dismissed on Thursday a news report claiming that Pakistan Air Force (PAF) aircraft were being used against the Yemen’s Houthis as “fake and fabricated”. A New York Times report published on Oct 7, a screenshot of which the ministry shared in an X post, cited an unnamed source as saying that PAF fighter jets were being employed against the group, amid the latter’s escalating conflict with Saudi Arabia.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Drones, explosions and soldiers in bulldozers: Surrounded by Israelis in Lebanon's 'model town'.
Dodging the broken glass carpeting her home in southern Lebanon, Mariam al-Yaghi exited onto her upper balcony and pointed. A few hundred metres ​away was a sight the 67-year-old had grown accustomed to: military vehicles moving through the adjacent Lebanese village, still occupied by Israeli troops. Mariam al-Yaghi ,67, Lebanese resident from West Zawtar, stands in her damaged house in southern Lebanon, on October 1, 2026. — Reuters At night, Israeli soldiers patrol so close to Yaghi’s home in ‌West Zawtar that she can hear their voices.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Bahrain working to 'speed up' approval of Pak-GCC free trade pact, foreign minister says.
Bahrain on Thursday said it was working to “speed up” the approval of a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). The remarks came after the two countries held the third session of their Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) in Islamabad. Bahrain’s FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani — who arrived in Pakistan last night on a two-day visit — co-chaired the JMC session along with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. Addressing a joint press briefing with Dar, the Bahraini minister noted that the JMC meeting covered “more than 15 fields”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: 9 terrorists killed in North Waziristan IBO: state media.
Security forces killed nine terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, state media reported on Wednesday. According to state-run Pakistan TV, IBOs were carried out in several areas of North Waziristan, including Palangzai, Nadeem Kot, and Kot Khazri, eliminating nine Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists, including four “important terrorist commanders”. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

Lenora Thaker wins $30,000 prize for ‘a work of state significance’ for The Pearl of Tagai Town, which draws on her family’s history in Cairns-Malay Town A “stunning” debut novel described as “unambiguously and distinctively Queensland” has won the $30,000 top prize at the Queensland literary awards (QLAs). Meriam and Wagedagam author Lenora Thaker won the Queensland premier’s award for a work of state significance for her historical novel The Pearl of Tagai Town, which was inspired by her ancestors’ lives in an unmapped shantytown known as Cairns-Malay Town.
